title.zh: 卷一百 表第一 諸王世表一
title.raw: 卷一百 表第一 諸王世表一 Volume 100 Tables 1: Princes 1

sentences.zh: 明太祖建藩，子孫世系預錫嘉名，以示傳世久遠。

translations.literal: The founding emperor of Ming established princely fiefs; successive generations of descendants were pre-granted auspicious names, to show that the line would be transmitted far into the future.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ming founder enfeoffed his sons as princes, he bestowed auspicious generational names on their descendants in advance, signifying that the house would endure for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 當神宗中葉，僅及祖訓之半，而不億之麗，宗祿虧乏，議者遂有減歲祿，限宮媵，且限支子之請。

translations.literal: At the middle of the Shenzong reign, [the clan] had reached only half of what the ancestral instructions foresaw, yet with uncountable numbers; clan stipends were depleted, and those who deliberated then proposed reducing annual stipends, limiting palace consorts, and also limiting petitions by collateral sons.
translations.idiomatic: By the mid-reign of Emperor Shenzong, the imperial clan had grown to only half the scale foreseen in the ancestral instructions—yet still to an uncountable multitude—and clan stipends ran short. Critics accordingly urged cuts to annual allotments, caps on palace consorts, and restrictions on petitions from collateral sons.

sentences.zh: 由是支屬承祧者，親王無旁推之恩；

translations.literal: From this, for collateral lines that succeeded to the sacrificial line, princes of the first rank had no grace of lateral succession;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth, when a collateral branch took over the main line, princes of the first rank were denied the former privilege of lateral succession;

sentences.zh: 群從繼世者，郡封絕再裂之例，以及名婚不時有明禁，本折互支屬常期。

translations.literal: for collateral kin who inherited the generation, enfeoffment as commandery prince cut off the precedent of a second partition, and there were also clear prohibitions on titled marriage at improper times—originally measures that cut against the regular expectation of mutual support among collateral branches.
translations.idiomatic: collateral heirs who took over a fief lost the old rule allowing a second split of commandery rank; explicit bans were also placed on titled marriages at improper times—policies that undercut the longstanding expectation that collateral branches would support one another.

sentences.zh: 啓、禎時，軍饷告絀，大農蒿目，安能顧瞻藩維。

translations.literal: In the Chongqi and Chongzhen reigns, military pay was reported exhausted; the Minister of Revenue gazed in distress—how could he still look after the feudatory bulwarks?
translations.idiomatic: Under the Chongqi and Chongzhen emperors, military funds ran dry and the Minister of Revenue could scarcely look on in despair, let alone spare thought for the princely fiefs.

sentences.zh: 親王或可自存，郡王以致中尉空乏尤甚。

translations.literal: Princes of the first rank might still support themselves, but from commandery princes down to assistant commandants, destitution was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: Princes of the first rank might still scrape by, but commandery princes and the lower ranks down to assistant commandant were plunged into the deepest want.

sentences.zh: 一旦盜起，無力禦侮，徒手就戮，宗社爲墟，惜哉！

translations.literal: Once bandits arose, [they] had no strength to repel insult; with bare hands they met slaughter, and altar and state became ruins—alas!
translations.idiomatic: When rebellion broke out at last, they lacked the means to defend themselves and were cut down unarmed; altar and state were laid waste—a tragedy indeed.

sentences.zh: 考之史冊，漢諸王表與王子侯離而不屬，世次難明。

translations.literal: Examining the historical records, in Han the table of kings and that of kings' sons and marquises were separate and not subordinated, and generations were hard to clarify.
translations.idiomatic: A look at earlier histories shows that in the Han dynasty the tables of kings and of kings' sons and marquises were kept apart rather than nested, making succession hard to follow.

sentences.zh: 唐宗族蕃大，源遠流長，然諸王以不出閤，不分房，子孫皆闕而不著。

translations.literal: In Tang the imperial clan flourished greatly, with source far and flow long; yet because princes did not leave the palace precinct and lineages were not divided into houses, descendants were all omitted and not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Tang the imperial clan grew vast over many generations, yet because princes never left the inner palace and lines were not sorted into houses, their descendants went unrecorded altogether.

sentences.zh: 宋史於太祖、太宗、魏王廷美之裔，迄臨安淪沒，悉載譜牒，而賢愚並列，漫無裁割。

translations.literal: The Song History, for descendants of Taizu, Taizong, and Prince Wei Tingmei, down to the fall of Lin'an, recorded all genealogies, but worthy and foolish were listed together without any pruning.
translations.idiomatic: The Song History listed every descendant of Taizu, Taizong, and Prince Wei Tingmei down to the fall of Lin'an, worthy and worthless alike, with no editorial selection.

sentences.zh: 茲表明代親王至郡王而止，以從史、漢諸王及王子侯之例。

translations.literal: This table lists Ming princes of the first rank down to commandery princes only, following the precedent of the History and of Han's tables of kings and of kings' sons and marquises.
translations.idiomatic: This table therefore records Ming princes of the first rank through commandery princes only, following the model of the Standard Histories and the Han tables of kings and of kings' sons and marquises.

sentences.zh: 又彷唐宗分房法，繫各府郡王於親王之下，如小宗之從大宗。

translations.literal: It also imitates the Tang method of dividing into houses, linking each prefecture's commandery princes under the prince of the first rank, as minor lines follow the major line.
translations.idiomatic: It also follows the Tang practice of sorting lines into houses, grouping each fief's commandery princes under their founding prince, as lesser lines attach to the main house.

sentences.zh: 其餘不得封者，概不載。

translations.literal: The rest who did not receive enfeoffment are in general not recorded.
translations.idiomatic: Those who never received a title are omitted entirely.

sentences.zh: （洪武中，太祖以子孫蕃衆，命名慮有重復，乃於東宮、親王世系，各擬二十字，字爲壹世。

translations.literal: (In the Hongwu reign, because descendants were numerous, the founder feared duplication in naming; he therefore for the Eastern Palace and each princely line drew up twenty characters, one character per generation.
translations.idiomatic: (During the Hongwu era, seeing how vast his posterity had become, the founder feared duplicate names and assigned twenty characters to the heir apparent and to each princely house—one character per generation.

sentences.zh: 子孫初生，宗人府依世次立雙名，以上壹字爲據，其下壹字則取五行偏旁者，以火、土、金、水、木爲序，惟靖江王不拘。

translations.literal: When descendants were first born, the Court of the Imperial Clan established a double name according to generation, taking the upper character as basis; the lower character then took the radical of the Five Phases, in the order fire, earth, metal, water, wood—only the Prince of Jingjiang was not bound by this.
translations.idiomatic: At birth the Court of the Imperial Clan assigned a two-character name by generation: the first character followed the prescribed series, and the second used radicals cycling through the Five Phases—fire, earth, metal, water, wood—except for the Jingjiang princely line, which was exempt.

sentences.zh: 東宮擬名曰：允文遵祖訓，欽武大君勝，順道宜逢吉，師良善用晟。

translations.literal: The Eastern Palace's proposed generational names: Yun Wen Zun Zu Xun, Qin Wu Da Jun Sheng, Shun Dao Yi Feng Ji, Shi Liang Shan Yong Sheng.
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent's twenty-character series was: Yun, Wen, Zun, Zu, Xun, Qin, Wu, Da, Jun, Sheng, Shun, Dao, Yi, Feng, Ji, Shi, Liang, Shan, Yong, Sheng.

sentences.zh: 秦府曰：尚志公誠秉，惟懷敬誼存，輔嗣資廉直，匡時永信敦。

translations.literal: The Qin princely house: Shang Zhi Gong Cheng Bing, Wei Huai Jing Yi Cun, Fu Si Zi Lian Zhi, Kuang Shi Yong Xin Dun.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin house used: Shang, Zhi, Gong, Cheng, Bing, Wei, Huai, Jing, Yi, Cun, Fu, Si, Zi, Lian, Zhi, Kuang, Shi, Yong, Xin, Dun.

sentences.zh: 晉府曰：濟美鍾奇表，知新慎敏求，審心鹹景慕，述學繼前修。

translations.literal: The Jin princely house: Ji Mei Zhong Qi Biao, Zhi Xin Shen Min Qiu, Shen Xin Xian Jing Mu, Shu Xue Ji Qian Xiu.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin house used: Ji, Mei, Zhong, Qi, Biao, Zhi, Xin, Shen, Min, Qiu, Shen, Xin, Xian, Jing, Mu, Shu, Xue, Ji, Qian, Xiu.

sentences.zh: 燕府後爲帝系，曰：高瞻祁見祐，厚載翊常由，慈和怡伯仲，簡靖迪先猷。

translations.literal: The Yan princely house, later the imperial line, said: Gao Zhan Qi Jian You, Hou Zai Yi Chang You, Ci He Yi Bo Zhong, Jian Jing Di Xian You.
translations.idiomatic: The Yan house, which later became the imperial line, used: Gao, Zhan, Qi, Jian, You, Hou, Zai, Yi, Chang, You, Ci, He, Yi, Bo, Zhong, Jian, Jing, Di, Xian, You.

sentences.zh: 周府曰：有子同安睦，勤朝在肅恭，紹倫敷惠潤，昭格廣登庸。

translations.literal: The Zhou princely house: You Zi Tong An Mu, Qin Chao Zai Su Gong, Shao Lun Fu Hui Run, Zhao Ge Guang Deng Yong.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou house used: You, Zi, Tong, An, Mu, Qin, Chao, Zai, Su, Gong, Shao, Lun, Fu, Hui, Run, Zhao, Ge, Guang, Deng, Yong.

sentences.zh: 楚府曰：孟季均榮顯，英華蘊盛容，宏才升博衍，茂士立全功。

translations.literal: The Chu princely house: Meng Ji Jun Rong Xian, Ying Hua Yun Sheng Rong, Hong Cai Sheng Bo Yan, Mao Shi Li Quan Gong.
translations.idiomatic: The Chu house used: Meng, Ji, Jun, Rong, Xian, Ying, Hua, Yun, Sheng, Rong, Hong, Cai, Sheng, Bo, Yan, Mao, Shi, Li, Quan, Gong.

sentences.zh: 齊府曰：賢能長可慶，睿智實堪宗，養性期淵雅，寅思復會通。

translations.literal: The Qi princely house: Xian Neng Chang Ke Qing, Rui Zhi Shi Kan Zong, Yang Xing Qi Yuan Ya, Yin Si Fu Hui Tong.
translations.idiomatic: The Qi house used: Xian, Neng, Chang, Ke, Qing, Rui, Zhi, Shi, Kan, Zong, Yang, Xing, Qi, Yuan, Ya, Yin, Si, Fu, Hui, Tong.

sentences.zh: 魯府曰：肇泰陽當健，觀頤壽以弘，振舉希兼達，康莊遇本甯。

translations.literal: The Lu princely house: Zhao Tai Yang Dang Jian, Guan Yi Shou Yi Hong, Zhen Ju Xi Jian Da, Kang Zhuang Yu Ben Ning.
translations.idiomatic: The Lu house used: Zhao, Tai, Yang, Dang, Jian, Guan, Yi, Shou, Yi, Hong, Zhen, Ju, Xi, Jian, Da, Kang, Zhuang, Yu, Ben, Ning.

sentences.zh: 蜀府曰：悅友申賓讓，承宣奉至平，懋進深滋益，端居務穆清。

translations.literal: The Shu princely house: Yue You Shen Bin Rang, Cheng Xuan Feng Zhi Ping, Mao Jin Shen Zi Yi, Duan Ju Wu Mu Qing.
translations.idiomatic: The Shu house used: Yue, You, Shen, Bin, Rang, Cheng, Xuan, Feng, Zhi, Ping, Mao, Jin, Shen, Zi, Yi, Duan, Ju, Wu, Mu, Qing.

sentences.zh: 湘府曰：久鎮開方嶽，揚威謹禮儀，剛毅循超卓，權衡素自持。

translations.literal: The Xiang princely house: Jiu Zhen Kai Fang Yue, Yang Wei Jin Li Yi, Gang Yi Xun Chao Zhuo, Quan Heng Su Zi Chi.
translations.idiomatic: The Xiang house used: Jiu, Zhen, Kai, Fang, Yue, Yang, Wei, Jin, Li, Yi, Gang, Yi, Xun, Chao, Zhuo, Quan, Heng, Su, Zi, Chi.

sentences.zh: 代府曰：遜仕成聦俊，充廷鼐鼎彜，傳贻連秀郁，炳燿壯洪基。

translations.literal: The Dai princely house: Xun Shi Cheng Cong Jun, Chong Ting Ding Ding Yi, Chuan Yi Lian Xiu Yu, Bing Yao Zhuang Hong Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Dai house used: Xun, Shi, Cheng, Cong, Jun, Chong, Ting, Ding, Ding, Yi, Chuan, Yi, Lian, Xiu, Yu, Bing, Yao, Zhuang, Hong, Ji.

sentences.zh: 肅府曰：瞻祿貢真弼，缙紳識烈忠，曦晖跻當運，凱谏處恒隆。

translations.literal: The Su princely house: Zhan Lu Gong Zhen Bi, Jin Shen Shi Lie Zhong, Xi Hui Ji Dang Yun, Kai Jian Chu Heng Long.
translations.idiomatic: The Su house used: Zhan, Lu, Gong, Zhen, Bi, Jin, Shen, Shi, Lie, Zhong, Xi, Hui, Ji, Dang, Yun, Kai, Jian, Chu, Heng, Long.

sentences.zh: 遼府曰：貴豪恩寵致，憲術俨尊儒，雲仍祺保合，操翰麗龍輿。

translations.literal: The Liao princely house: Gui Hao En Chong Zhi, Xian Shu Yan Zun Ru, Yun Reng Qi Bao He, Cao Han Li Long Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Liao house used: Gui, Hao, En, Chong, Zhi, Xian, Shu, Yan, Zun, Ru, Yun, Reng, Qi, Bao, He, Cao, Han, Li, Long, Yu.

sentences.zh: 慶府曰：秩邃寘台鼒，倪伸帥倬奇，適完因巨衎，骘眷發需毘。

translations.literal: The Qing princely house: Zhi Sui Zhi Tai Zi, Ni Shen Shu Zhuo Qi, Shi Wan Yin Ju Kan, Zhi Juan Fa Xu Pi.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing house used: Zhi, Sui, Zhi, Tai, Zi, Ni, Shen, Shu, Zhuo, Qi, Shi, Wan, Yin, Ju, Kan, Zhi, Juan, Fa, Xu, Pi.

sentences.zh: 甯府曰：磐奠觐辰拱，多謀統議中，總添支庶闊，作哲向親衷。

translations.literal: The Ning princely house: Pan Dian Jin Chen Gong, Duo Mou Tong Yi Zhong, Zong Tian Zhi Shu Kuo, Zuo Zhe Xiang Qin Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: The Ning house used: Pan, Dian, Jin, Chen, Gong, Duo, Mou, Tong, Yi, Zhong, Zong, Tian, Zhi, Shu, Kuo, Zuo, Zhe, Xiang, Qin, Zhong.

sentences.zh: 岷府曰：徽音膺彥譽，定幹企禋雍，崇理原谘訪，寬鎔喜贲從。

translations.literal: The Min princely house: Hui Yin Ying Yan Yu, Ding Gan Qi Yin Yong, Chong Li Yuan Zi Fang, Kuan Rong Xi Ben Cong.
translations.idiomatic: The Min house used: Hui, Yin, Ying, Yan, Yu, Ding, Gan, Qi, Yin, Yong, Chong, Li, Yuan, Zi, Fang, Kuan, Rong, Xi, Ben, Cong.

sentences.zh: 谷府曰：賦質僖雄敞，叢興闡福昌，笃諧恂怿豫，擴霁昱祯祥。

translations.literal: The Gu princely house: Fu Zhi Xi Xiong Chang, Cong Xing Chan Fu Chang, Du Xie Xun Yi Yu, Kuo Ji Yu Zhen Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Gu house used: Fu, Zhi, Xi, Xiong, Chang, Cong, Xing, Chan, Fu, Chang, Du, Xie, Xun, Yi, Yu, Kuo, Ji, Yu, Zhen, Xiang.

sentences.zh: 韓府曰：沖範徵偕旭，融谟朗璟逵，亶韶愉灏造，令緒價蕃維。

translations.literal: The Han princely house: Chong Fan Zheng Xie Xu, Rong Mo Lang Jing Kui, Dan Shao Yu Hao Zao, Ling Xu Jia Fan Wei.
translations.idiomatic: The Han house used: Chong, Fan, Zheng, Xie, Xu, Rong, Mo, Lang, Jing, Kui, Dan, Shao, Yu, Hao, Zao, Ling, Xu, Jia, Fan, Wei.

sentences.zh: 沈府曰：佶幼诠勳允，恬呈效回皇，是源諲晳暐，圭璧澈澄昂。

translations.literal: The Shen princely house: Ji You Quan Xun Yun, Tian Cheng Xiao Hui Huang, Shi Yuan Yin Xi Wei, Gui Bi Che Cheng Ang.
translations.idiomatic: The Shen house used: Ji, You, Quan, Xun, Yun, Tian, Cheng, Xiao, Hui, Huang, Shi, Yuan, Yin, Xi, Wei, Gui, Bi, Che, Cheng, Ang.

sentences.zh: 安府曰：斐序斌廷賞，凝覃浚祉襄，恢嚴颛輯矩，缜密廓程綱。

translations.literal: The An princely house: Fei Xu Bin Ting Shang, Ning Tan Jun Zhi Xiang, Hui Yan Zhuan Ji Ju, Zhen Mi Kuo Cheng Gang.
translations.idiomatic: The An house used: Fei, Xu, Bin, Ting, Shang, Ning, Tan, Jun, Zhi, Xiang, Hui, Yan, Zhuan, Ji, Ju, Zhen, Mi, Kuo, Cheng, Gang.

sentences.zh: 唐府曰：瓊芝彌宇宙，碩器聿琳據，啓齡蒙頌體，嘉曆協銘圖。

translations.literal: The Tang princely house: Qiong Zhi Mi Yu Zhou, Shuo Qi Yu Lin Ju, Qi Ling Meng Song Ti, Jia Li Xie Ming Tu.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang house used: Qiong, Zhi, Mi, Yu, Zhou, Shuo, Qi, Yu, Lin, Ju, Qi, Ling, Meng, Song, Ti, Jia, Li, Xie, Ming, Tu.

sentences.zh: 郢府曰：偉聞參望奭，箴誨咱臯夔，麒麟余積兆，奎頴晔璿玑。

translations.literal: The Ying princely house: Wei Wen Can Wang Shi, Zhen Hui Za Gao Kui, Qi Lin Yu Ji Zhao, Kui Ying Ye Xuan Ji.
translations.idiomatic: The Ying house used: Wei, Wen, Can, Wang, Shi, Zhen, Hui, Za, Gao, Kui, Qi, Lin, Yu, Ji, Zhao, Kui, Ying, Ye, Xuan, Ji.

sentences.zh: 伊府曰：顒勉堤訏典，襃珂采鳳琛，應疇頒胄選，昆玉冠泉金。

translations.literal: The Yi princely house: Yong Mian Di Xu Dian, Bao Ke Cai Feng Chen, Ying Chou Ban Zhou Xuan, Kun Yu Guan Quan Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The Yi house used: Yong, Mian, Di, Xu, Dian, Bao, Ke, Cai, Feng, Chen, Ying, Chou, Ban, Zhou, Xuan, Kun, Yu, Guan, Quan, Jin.

sentences.zh: 靖江王曰：贊佐相規約，經邦任履亨，若依純壹行，遠得襲芳名。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingjiang: Zan Zuo Xiang Gui Yue, Jing Bang Ren Lü Heng, Ruo Yi Chun Yi Xing, Yuan De Xi Fang Ming.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingjiang princely line used: Zan, Zuo, Xiang, Gui, Yue, Jing, Bang, Ren, Lü, Heng, Ruo, Yi, Chun, Yi, Xing, Yuan, De, Xi, Fang, Ming.

sentences.zh: 考明代帝系，熹宗、莊烈二帝名，始及「由」字。

translations.literal: Examining the Ming imperial line, the names of the two emperors Xizong and Zhuanglie first reached the character You.
translations.idiomatic: In the Ming imperial line, only under the Xizong and Chongzhen emperors did reign names reach the character You in the generational series.

sentences.zh: 其他王府，亦多不出十字。

translations.literal: Other princely houses also for the most part did not go beyond ten characters.
translations.idiomatic: Most other princely houses likewise never used more than ten of their twenty characters.

sentences.zh: 親王之子，例封郡王。

translations.literal: Sons of princes of the first rank were by rule enfeoffed as commandery princes.
translations.idiomatic: Sons of a prince of the first rank were routinely enfeoffed as commandery princes.

sentences.zh: 若以支屬嗣者，自後長子襲封親王外，餘子仍照原封世次，授以本等爵級，不得冒濫郡爵。

translations.literal: If a collateral line succeeded, thereafter apart from the eldest son inheriting as prince of the first rank, the remaining sons still followed the original enfeoffment generation and were granted their proper rank, and might not usurp commandery titles.
translations.idiomatic: When a collateral branch took over a princely fief, only the eldest son could inherit as prince of the first rank; other sons kept the ranks appropriate to their original line and could not improperly claim commandery titles.

sentences.zh: 郡王無字，兄弟及兄弟之子不得請襲，違者爲冒封。

translations.literal: Commandery princes had no generational characters; brothers and brothers' sons might not petition to inherit—violators were deemed usurpers of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery princes had no generational name series; brothers and their sons could not petition to succeed the title, and to do so counted as fraudulent enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 皆萬曆七年例也。

translations.literal: All were precedents of the seventh year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: These were all regulations of the seventh year of Wanli (1579).

sentences.zh: ） 太祖二十六子。

translations.literal: ) The founder had twenty-six sons.
translations.idiomatic: ) The founding emperor had twenty-six sons.

sentences.zh: 懿文太子外，皇子楠未封。

translations.literal: Apart from the heir apparent Yiwen, the prince Nan was not enfeoffed.
translations.idiomatic: Aside from Crown Prince Yiwen, the prince Nan received no enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 成祖以洪武三年封燕王，後尊爲帝系，不得仍列之藩封世次。

translations.literal: Chengzu was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan in the third year of Hongwu; later he was honored as the imperial line and could not still be listed in the generations of feudatory enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzu was made Prince of Yan in Hongwu year 3 and later became the imperial line, so he is not listed among the feudatory successions.

sentences.zh: 其得封者二十三王，曰秦愍王樉，曰晉恭王棡，曰周定王橚，曰楚昭王楨，曰齊王榑，曰潭王梓，曰趙王杞，曰魯荒王檀，曰蜀獻王椿，曰湘獻王柏，曰代簡王桂，曰肅莊王楧，曰遼簡王植，曰慶靖王㮵，曰甯獻王全，曰岷莊王便，曰谷王橞，曰韓憲王松，曰沈簡王模，曰安惠王楹，曰唐定王桱，曰郢靖王棟，曰伊厲王㰘。

translations.literal: Those who received enfeoffment were twenty-three kings: called Prince Min of Qin, Shuang; Prince Gong of Jin, Gang; Prince Ding of Zhou, Su; Prince Zhao of Chu, Zhen; Prince of Qi, Fu; Prince of Tan, Zi; Prince of Zhao, Qi; Prince Huang of Lu, Tan; Prince Xian of Shu, Chun; Prince Xian of Xiang, Bai; Prince Jian of Dai, Gui; Prince Zhuang of Su, Zhen; Prince Jian of Liao, Zhi; Prince Jing of Qing, ?; Prince Xian of Ning, Quan; Prince Zhuang of Min, Bian; Prince of Gu, ?; Prince Xian of Han, Song; Prince Jian of Shen, Mo; Prince Hui of An, Ying; Prince Ding of Tang, ?; Prince Jing of Ying, Dong; Prince Li of Yi, ?.
translations.idiomatic: Twenty-three received princely titles: Prince Min of Qin (Shuang), Prince Gong of Jin (Gang), Prince Ding of Zhou (Su), Prince Zhao of Chu (Zhen), Prince of Qi (Fu), Prince of Tan (Zi), Prince of Zhao (Qi), Prince Huang of Lu (Tan), Prince Xian of Shu (Chun), Prince Xian of Xiang (Bai), Prince Jian of Dai (Gui), Prince Zhuang of Su (Zhen), Prince Jian of Liao (Zhi), Prince Jing of Qing, Prince Xian of Ning (Quan), Prince Zhuang of Min (Bian), Prince of Gu, Prince Xian of Han (Song), Prince Jian of Shen (Mo), Prince Hui of An (Ying), Prince Ding of Tang, Prince Jing of Ying (Dong), and Prince Li of Yi.

sentences.zh: 而靖江王以南昌嫡孫受封郡王，附載於後。

translations.literal: The Prince of Jingjiang, as eldest grandson by the principal line of Nanchang, received enfeoffment as commandery prince and is appended at the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Jingjiang prince, enfeoffed as a commandery prince in his capacity as principal grandson of the Nanchang line, is recorded afterward.

sentences.zh: rowspan="11" valign="top"|秦 愍王樉，太祖嫡二子，洪武三年封。十一年就藩西安府。二十八年薨。

translations.literal: Qin: Prince Min Shuang, the founder's second son by the principal consort, enfeoffed in the third year of Hongwu. In the eleventh year he went to his fief at Xi'an prefecture. He died in the twenty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Qin: Prince Min Shuang, the founder's second son by his principal consort, was enfeoffed in Hongwu 3, took up his fief at Xi'an in Hongwu 11, and died in Hongwu 28.

sentences.zh: 隱王尚炳，愍嫡一子，洪武二十八年襲封。永樂十年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Yin Shangbing, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Min, inherited the fief in the twenty-eighth year of Hongwu. He died in the tenth year of Yongle.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yin Shangbing, Prince Min's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Hongwu 28 and died in Yongle 10.

sentences.zh: 僖王志堩，隱嫡一子，永樂十年襲封。二十二年未娶薨。 懷王志均，隱庶二子，初封渭南王，永樂二十二年進封。宣德元年未娶薨。 康王志𡐤，隱庶三子，初封富平王，宣德三年進封。景泰六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Xi Zhiheng, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Yin, inherited in the tenth year of Yongle. In the twenty-second year he died unmarried. Prince Huai Zhi Jun, the second son by a secondary consort of Prince Yin, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Weinan and advanced in the twenty-second year of Yongle. In the first year of Xuande he died unmarried. Prince Kang Zhi ?, the third son by a secondary consort of Prince Yin, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Fuping and advanced in the third year of Xuande. He died in the sixth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xi Zhiheng, Prince Yin's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Yongle 10 and died unmarried in Yongle 22. Prince Huai Zhi Jun, Prince Yin's second son by a concubine, was first made Prince of Weinan and promoted in Yongle 22; he died unmarried in Xuande 1. Prince Kang, Prince Yin's third son by a concubine, was first Prince of Fuping, promoted in Xuande 3, and died in Jingtai 6.

sentences.zh: 惠王公錫，康嫡一子，天順二年襲封。成化二十二年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Hui Gong Xi, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Kang, inherited in the second year of Tianshun. He died in the twenty-second year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Hui Gong Xi, Prince Kang's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Tianshun 2 and died in Chenghua 22.

sentences.zh: 簡王誠泳，惠庶一子，成化四年封鎮安王，弘治元年襲封秦王。十一年薨。無子。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Cheng Yong, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Hui, was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhen'an in the fourth year of Chenghua and inherited as Prince of Qin in the first year of Hongzhi. He died in the eleventh year. He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Cheng Yong, Prince Hui's only son by a concubine, was made Prince of Zhen'an in Chenghua 4, succeeded as Prince of Qin in Hongzhi 1, died in Hongzhi 11, and left no heir.

sentences.zh: 昭王秉欆，簡從弟臨潼王誠澯庶一子，初襲臨潼王，弘治十三年嗣封秦王。追諡其祖公銘為安王，父誠澯為莊王。十四年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Bing ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Cheng Zao of Lintong, a younger cousin of Prince Jian, first inherited as Prince of Lintong; in the thirteenth year of Hongzhi he succeeded as Prince of Qin. His grandfather Gong Ming was posthumously titled Prince An, and his father Cheng Zao Prince Zhuang. He died in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Bing ?, sole son by a concubine of Prince Cheng Zao of Lintong (Prince Jian's younger cousin), first held Lintong and in Hongzhi 13 succeeded to Qin; his grandfather Gong Ming and father Cheng Zao were posthumously titled Princes An and Zhuang. He died in Hongzhi 14.

sentences.zh: 定王惟焯，昭庶一子，正德四年襲封。嘉靖二十三年薨。無子。

translations.literal: Prince Ding Wei ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhao, inherited in the fourth year of Zhengde. He died in the twenty-third year of Jiajing. He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding Wei ?, Prince Zhao's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Zhengde 4, died in Jiajing 23, and left no heir.

sentences.zh: 宣王懷埢，定再從弟奉國將軍惟燫之子，初封鎮國中尉，嘉靖二十七年嗣封秦王。追諡其曾祖鎮國將軍誠潤為恭王，祖輔國將軍秉柎為順王，父惟燫為端王。誠潤，安庶二子也。四十五年，宣王薨。

translations.literal: Prince Xuan Huai ?, son of Supporter-of-the-State General Wei ?, a second cousin once removed of Prince Ding, was first enfeoffed as Defender-of-the-State Assistant Commandant; in the twenty-seventh year of Jiajing he succeeded as Prince of Qin. His great-grandfather Defender-of-the-State General Cheng Run was posthumously titled Prince Gong, his grandfather Supporter-of-the-State General Bing ? Prince Shun, and his father Wei ? Prince Duan. Cheng Run was the second son by a secondary consort of Prince An. In the forty-fifth year Prince Xuan died.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xuan Huai ?, son of Supporter-of-the-State General Wei ? (a distant cousin of Prince Ding), was first a Defender-of-the-State assistant commandant and in Jiajing 27 succeeded to Qin; his forebears Cheng Run, Bing ?, and Wei ? were posthumously titled Princes Gong, Shun, and Duan. Cheng Run was Prince An's second son by a concubine. Prince Xuan died in Jiajing 45.

sentences.zh: 靖王敬鎔，宣庶一子，初封隆德王，隆慶三年襲封。萬曆四年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Jing ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Xuan, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Longde; in the third year of Longqing he inherited the fief. He died in the fourth year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Jing ?, Prince Xuan's only son by a concubine, was first Prince of Longde, succeeded in Longqing 3, and died in Wanli 4.

sentences.zh: 敬王誼澏，靖嫡一子，萬曆三年封世子，九年襲封。十四年薨。無子。王誼漶，靖嫡三子，萬曆十三年襲封奉國中尉，十四年加封紫陽王，十五年進封。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Yi ?, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Jing, was made heir in the third year of Wanli and inherited in the ninth year. He died in the fourteenth year. He had no sons. Prince Yi ?, the third son by the principal consort of Prince Jing, inherited as Supporter-of-the-State Assistant Commandant in the thirteenth year of Wanli, was additionally enfeoffed as Prince of Ziyang in the fourteenth year, and advanced in the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Yi ?, Prince Jing's eldest son by his principal consort, was named heir in Wanli 3, succeeded in Wanli 9, and died childless in Wanli 14. Prince Yi ?, Prince Jing's third son by his principal consort, became a Supporter-of-the-State assistant commandant in Wanli 13, was made Prince of Ziyang in Wanli 14, and promoted in Wanli 15.

sentences.zh: 存樞，誼漶子，萬曆年襲封。崇禎末陷於賊。

translations.literal: Cun Shu, son of Yi ?, inherited in a Wanli year. At the end of Chongzhen he fell into the hands of bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Cun Shu, son of Yi ?, succeeded during the Wanli reign and at the end of Chongzhen was captured by rebels.

cells.content: 永興 懿簡王尚烈，愍嫡二子，永樂元年封。十五年薨。

translations.literal: Yongxing: Prince Yi Jian Shanglie, the second son by the principal consort of Prince Min, was enfeoffed in the first year of Yongle. He died in the fifteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Yongxing: Prince Yi Jian Shanglie, Prince Min's second son by his principal consort, was enfeoffed in Yongle 1 and died in Yongle 15.

cells.literal: Yongxing: Prince Yi Jian Shanglie, the second son by the principal consort of Prince Min, was enfeoffed in the first year of Yongle. He died in the fifteenth year.
cells.idiomatic: Yongxing: Prince Yi Jian Shanglie, Prince Min's second son by his principal consort, was enfeoffed in Yongle 1 and died in Yongle 15.
cells.translation: Yongxing: Prince Yi Jian Shanglie, Prince Min's second son by his principal consort, was enfeoffed in Yongle 1 and died in Yongle 15.

cells.content: 恭憲王志㙸，懿簡庶一子，永樂二十年襲封。景泰五年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Xian Zhi ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Yi Jian, inherited in the twentieth year of Yongle. He died in the fifth year of Jingtai.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Xian Zhi ?, Prince Yi Jian's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Yongle 20 and died in Jingtai 5.

cells.content: 昭僖王公鉐，恭憲庶一子，景泰六年襲封。弘治元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zhao Xi Gong ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Gong Xian, inherited in the sixth year of Jingtai. He died in the first year of Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Xi Gong ?, Prince Gong Xian's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Jingtai 6 and died in Hongzhi 1.

cells.literal: Prince Zhao Xi Gong ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Gong Xian, inherited in the sixth year of Jingtai. He died in the first year of Hongzhi.
cells.idiomatic: Prince Zhao Xi Gong ?, Prince Gong Xian's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Jingtai 6 and died in Hongzhi 1.
cells.translation: Prince Zhao Xi Gong ?, Prince Gong Xian's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Jingtai 6 and died in Hongzhi 1.

cells.content: 榮惠王誠瀾，昭僖嫡一子，弘治四年襲封。正德二年薨。二子俱殀。

translations.literal: Prince Rong Hui Cheng Lan, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Zhao Xi, inherited in the fourth year of Hongzhi. He died in the second year of Zhengde. Both sons died young.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong Hui Cheng Lan, Prince Zhao Xi's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Hongzhi 4, died in Zhengde 2, and both his sons died in infancy.

cells.literal: Prince Rong Hui Cheng Lan, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Zhao Xi, inherited in the fourth year of Hongzhi. He died in the second year of Zhengde. Both sons died young.
cells.idiomatic: Prince Rong Hui Cheng Lan, Prince Zhao Xi's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Hongzhi 4, died in Zhengde 2, and both his sons died in infancy.
cells.translation: Prince Rong Hui Cheng Lan, Prince Zhao Xi's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Hongzhi 4, died in Zhengde 2, and both his sons died in infancy.

cells.content: 莊定王秉櫸，榮惠從姪，正德六年以奉國將軍嗣封。嘉靖十二年薨。王以從姪由將軍進封，據例為冒。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Ding Bing ?, a nephew of Prince Rong Hui, succeeded as Supporter-of-the-State General in the sixth year of Zhengde. He died in the twelfth year of Jiajing. Because the prince as nephew advanced from general to enfeoffment, by precedent this was deemed usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang Ding Bing ?, a nephew of Prince Rong Hui, succeeded in Zhengde 6 from the rank of Supporter-of-the-State general and died in Jiajing 12. His promotion from general to prince as a collateral nephew was ruled a usurpation under precedent.

cells.literal: Prince Zhuang Ding Bing ?, a nephew of Prince Rong Hui, succeeded as Supporter-of-the-State General in the sixth year of Zhengde. He died in the twelfth year of Jiajing. Because the prince as nephew advanced from general to enfeoffment, by precedent this was deemed usurpation.

cells.content: 恭定王惟熣，莊定庶一子，嘉靖十七年襲封。萬曆二年薨。王自首冒封，不再襲，除。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Ding Wei ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhuang Ding, inherited in the seventeenth year of Jiajing. He died in the second year of Wanli. The prince confessed to usurped enfeoffment; [the line] was not to inherit again and was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Ding Wei ?, Prince Zhuang Ding's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Jiajing 17 and died in Wanli 2. He confessed to fraudulent enfeoffment; the line was barred from further succession and abolished.

cells.literal: Prince Gong Ding Wei ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhuang Ding, inherited in the seventeenth year of Jiajing. He died in the second year of Wanli. The prince confessed to usurped enfeoffment; [the line] was not to inherit again and was abolished.

cells.content: 保安 懷僖王尚煜，愍嫡三子，永樂元年封。七年薨。

translations.literal: Bao'an: Prince Huai Xi Shangyu, the third son by the principal consort of Prince Min, was enfeoffed in the first year of Yongle. He died in the seventh year.
translations.idiomatic: Bao'an: Prince Huai Xi Shangyu, Prince Min's third son by his principal consort, was enfeoffed in Yongle 1 and died in Yongle 7.

cells.content: 悼順王志垌，懷僖庶一子，永樂十九年襲封。正統元年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Dao Shun Zhi ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Huai Xi, inherited in the nineteenth year of Yongle. He died in the first year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Dao Shun Zhi ?, Prince Huai Xi's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Yongle 19 and died in Zhengtong 1.

cells.literal: Prince Dao Shun Zhi ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Huai Xi, inherited in the nineteenth year of Yongle. He died in the first year of Zhengtong.

cells.content: 莊簡王公鍊，悼順嫡一子，正統十一年襲封。成化十一年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Jian Gong ?, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Dao Shun, inherited in the eleventh year of Zhengtong. He died in the eleventh year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang Jian Gong ?, Prince Dao Shun's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Zhengtong 11 and died in Chenghua 11.

cells.literal: Prince Zhuang Jian Gong ?, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Dao Shun, inherited in the eleventh year of Zhengtong. He died in the eleventh year of Chenghua.

cells.content: 榮穆王誠潢，莊簡嫡一子，成化十四年襲封。弘治八年薨。無子。 昭和王誠淥，莊簡庶一子，弘治十年以鎮國將軍進封。十四年薨。無子。靖和王誠漖，莊簡庶二子，正德三年以鎮國將軍進封。十四年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Rong Mu Cheng Huang, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Zhuang Jian, inherited in the fourteenth year of Chenghua. He died in the eighth year of Hongzhi. He had no sons. Prince Zhao He Cheng Lu, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhuang Jian, was advanced from Defender-of-the-State General in the tenth year of Hongzhi. He died in the fourteenth year. He had no sons. Prince Jing He Cheng Jiao, the second son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhuang Jian, was advanced from Defender-of-the-State General in the third year of Zhengde. He died in the fourteenth year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Rong Mu Cheng Huang, Prince Zhuang Jian's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Chenghua 14, died in Hongzhi 8, and left no heir. Prince Zhao He Cheng Lu, Prince Zhuang Jian's only son by a concubine, was promoted from defender-of-the-state general in Hongzhi 10 and died childless in Hongzhi 14. Prince Jing He Cheng Jiao, Prince Zhuang Jian's second son by a concubine, was promoted from defender-of-the-state general in Zhengde 3 and died in Zhengde 14.

cells.content: 恭懿王秉棧，靖和庶一子，嘉靖六年以鎮國將軍襲封。因王父冒封，例不再襲，除。

translations.literal: Prince Gong Yi Bing ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Jing He, inherited as Defender-of-the-State General in the sixth year of Jiajing. Because the prince's father had usurped enfeoffment, by precedent [the line] was not to inherit again and was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong Yi Bing ?, Prince Jing He's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Jiajing 6 from defender-of-the-state rank, but because his father had usurped the title the line was abolished and barred from further succession.

cells.content: 興平 恭靖王尚烐，愍庶四子，永樂初封。正統十四年薨。

translations.literal: Xingping: Prince Gong Jing Shang ?, the fourth son by a secondary consort of Prince Min, was enfeoffed at the beginning of Yongle. He died in the fourteenth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: Xingping: Prince Gong Jing Shang ?, Prince Min's fourth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed early in Yongle and died in Zhengtong 14.

cells.content: 莊惠王志㙞，恭靖嫡一子，景泰三年襲封。天順元年薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Hui Zhi ?, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Gong Jing, inherited in the third year of Jingtai. He died in the first year of Tianshun. He had no sons; [the line was] abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zhuang Hui Zhi ?, Prince Gong Jing's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Jingtai 3, died in Tianshun 1 without heirs, and the line was abolished.

cells.content: 永壽 懷簡王尚灴，愍庶五子，永樂初封。十八年薨。安惠王志埴，懷簡嫡一子，宣德六年襲封。成化六年薨。

translations.literal: Yongshou: Prince Huai Jian Shang ?, the fifth son by a secondary consort of Prince Min, was enfeoffed at the beginning of Yongle. He died in the eighteenth year. Prince An Hui Zhi ?, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Huai Jian, inherited in the sixth year of Xuande. He died in the sixth year of Chenghua.
translations.idiomatic: Yongshou: Prince Huai Jian Shang ?, Prince Min's fifth son by a concubine, was enfeoffed early in Yongle and died in Yongle 18. Prince An Hui Zhi ?, his only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Xuande 6 and died in Chenghua 6.

cells.content: 恭和王秉欓，莊僖庶一子，弘治十年以鎮國將軍襲封。嘉靖十七年薨。庶一子惟燿先卒，庶六子惟燱以母邵氏封妃，自謂嫡子當立，請襲得允。後惟燿子懷墡奏辨。會議以邵氏因內助進封，惟燱不得稱嫡，乃以懷墡襲封。

translations.literal: Prince Gong He Bing ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhuang Xi, inherited as Defender-of-the-State General in the tenth year of Hongzhi. He died in the seventeenth year of Jiajing. The first son by a secondary consort, Wei Yao, died first. The sixth son by a secondary consort, Wei ?, because his mother Lady Shao was enfeoffed as consort, claimed himself the son by the principal consort who ought to succeed and petitioned to inherit and was approved. Later Wei Yao's son Huai ? memorialized to dispute. At conference it was held that because Lady Shao had been advanced to consort through inner favor, Wei ? could not be called son by the principal consort, and therefore Huai ? inherited.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gong He Bing ?, Prince Zhuang Xi's only son by a concubine, succeeded in Hongzhi 10 from defender-of-the-state rank and died in Jiajing 17. His first son by a concubine, Wei Yao, had died earlier; his sixth son, Wei ?, whose mother Lady Shao had been raised to consort through palace influence, claimed legitimacy as principal heir and was initially allowed to succeed. Later Wei Yao's son Huai ? petitioned for redress. The court ruled that Lady Shao's elevation did not make Wei ? a principal son, and Huai ? was granted the succession.

cells.content: rowspan="25" valign="top"|晉 恭王棡，太祖嫡三子，洪武三年封。十一年就藩太原府。三十一年薨。

translations.literal: Jin: Prince Gong Gang, the founder's third son by the principal consort, was enfeoffed in the third year of Hongwu. In the eleventh year he went to his fief at Taiyuan prefecture. He died in the thirty-first year.
translations.idiomatic: Jin: Prince Gong Gang, the founder's third son by his principal consort, was enfeoffed in Hongwu 3, took up his fief at Taiyuan in Hongwu 11, and died in Hongwu 31.

cells.content: 定王濟熺，恭嫡一子，洪武三十一年襲封。永樂十二年為弟濟熿誣搆，廢守恭王墳園。後事明，仁宗賜王冠服，令依子美圭養。宣德十年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Ding Ji Xi, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Gong, inherited in the thirty-first year of Hongwu. In the twelfth year of Yongle he was framed by his younger brother Ji Huang and deposed to guard Prince Gong's tomb park. Later he was cleared; Renzong bestowed princely robes and ordered that he be supported according to his son Mei Gui. He died in the tenth year of Xuande.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Ding Ji Xi, Prince Gong's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Hongwu 31. In Yongle 12 his younger brother Ji Huang framed him and he was deposed to guard Prince Gong's tomb. Later exonerated, Renzong granted him princely regalia and ordered support according to his son Mei Gui. He died in Xuande 10.

cells.content: 憲王美圭，定嫡一子，永樂三年封世子，為叔濟熿誣廢，隨父守墳。二十一年事明，封平陽王。宣德十年襲封晉王。正統六年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Xian Mei Gui, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Ding, was made heir in the third year of Yongle; he was falsely deposed by his uncle Ji Huang and followed his father in guarding the tomb. In the twenty-first year he was cleared and enfeoffed as Prince of Pingyang. In the tenth year of Xuande he inherited as Prince of Jin. He died in the sixth year of Zhengtong.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xian Mei Gui, Prince Ding's only son by his principal consort, was named heir in Yongle 3 but was deposed on his uncle Ji Huang's false accusation and joined his father at the tomb. Cleared in Yongle 21, he was made Prince of Pingyang and in Xuande 10 succeeded to Jin. He died in Zhengtong 6.

cells.content: 莊王鍾鉉，憲庶一子，初封榆社王，正統七年襲封。弘治十五年薨。曾孫知烊立。

translations.literal: Prince Zhuang Zhong Xuan, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Xian, was first enfeoffed as Prince of Yushe and inherited the fief in the seventh year of Zhengtong. He died in the fifteenth year of Hongzhi. His great-grandson Zhi Yang succeeded.

cells.content: 奇源，莊嫡一子，天順三年封世子。弘治十四年薨。以孫知烊襲封，追封王，諡曰靖。

translations.literal: Qi Yuan, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Zhuang, was made heir in the third year of Tianshun. He died in the fourteenth year of Hongzhi. His grandson Zhi Yang inherited the fief; [Qi Yuan] was posthumously enfeoffed as prince with the posthumous title Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Qi Yuan, Prince Zhuang's only son by his principal consort, was named heir in Tianshun 3. He died in Hongzhi 14. His grandson Zhi Yang succeeded; Qi Yuan was posthumously made prince with the title Jing.

cells.content: 表榮，靖嫡一子，成化十四年封世孫。弘治六年薨。以子知烊襲封，追封王，諡曰懷。

translations.literal: Biao Rong, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Jing, was made heir-apparent in the fourteenth year of Chenghua. He died in the sixth year of Hongzhi. His son Zhi Yang inherited the fief; [Biao Rong] was posthumously enfeoffed as prince with the posthumous title Huai.

translations.literal: Prince Duan Zhi Yang, the second son by a secondary consort of Prince Huai, was made heir-great-great-grandson in the eleventh year of Hongzhi and inherited in the sixteenth year. He died in the twelfth year of Jiajing. He had no sons.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Duan Zhi Yang, Prince Huai's second son by a secondary consort, was named heir-great-great-grandson in Hongzhi 11 and succeeded in Hongzhi 16. He died in Jiajing 12 without issue.

cells.content: 簡王新㙉，端從弟新化王知㸅庶一子，嘉靖十二年以新化王長子奉敕管理府事。十五年嗣封晉王。追諡其祖秉槏為安王，父知㸅為康王。萬曆三年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jian Xin ?, a younger cousin once removed of Prince Duan and the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhi ? of Xinhua, in the twelfth year of Jiajing was ordered by imperial decree as eldest son of the Prince of Xinhua to administer the princely household. In the fifteenth year he succeeded as Prince of Jin. His grandfather Bing ? was posthumously titled Prince An and his father Zhi ? Prince Kang. He died in the third year of Wanli.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jian Xin ?, Prince Duan's younger cousin once removed and the only son by a secondary consort of Prince Zhi ? of Xinhua, was ordered in Jiajing 12 as the Xinhua heir to administer the household. In Jiajing 15 he succeeded to Jin. His grandfather Bing ? was posthumously titled Prince An and his father Zhi ? Prince Kang. He died in Wanli 3.

cells.content: 敬王慎鏡，簡親弟鎮國將軍新墧嫡一子，初封輔國將軍。萬曆四年奉敕管理府事。六年卒。七年追封，加諡。無子。 惠王慎鋷，新墧嫡三子，敬親弟，嘉靖三十年封輔國將軍。萬曆七年進封。本年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Jing Shen Jing, a full younger brother of Prince Jian and the lone son by the principal consort of Supporter-of-the-State General Xin ?, was first enfeoffed as Defender-of-the-State General. In the fourth year of Wanli he was ordered by imperial decree to administer the princely household. He died in the sixth year; in the seventh year he was posthumously enfeoffed and given a posthumous title. He had no sons. Prince Hui Shen ?, the third son by the principal consort of Xin ? and full younger brother of Prince Jing, was enfeoffed as Defender-of-the-State General in the thirtieth year of Jiajing. He advanced to the fief in the seventh year of Wanli and died in that same year.

cells.content: 穆王敏淳，惠嫡一子，萬曆十三年襲封。三十八年薨。

translations.literal: Prince Mu Min Chun, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Hui, inherited in the thirteenth year of Wanli. He died in the thirty-eighth year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Mu Min Chun, Prince Hui's only son by his principal consort, succeeded in Wanli 13 and died in Wanli 38.

cells.content: 王求桂，穆庶一子，萬曆三十九年請敕管理府事。四十一年襲封。崇禎末陷於賊。

translations.literal: Prince Qiu Gui, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Mu, requested and received an imperial decree to administer the princely household in the thirty-ninth year of Wanli and inherited in the forty-first year. At the end of the Chongzhen reign he fell to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Qiu Gui, Prince Mu's only son by a secondary consort, was granted decree to administer the household in Wanli 39 and succeeded in Wanli 41. At the end of Chongzhen he fell to the rebels.

cells.content: 高平 懷簡王濟燁，恭庶二子，永樂初封。五年薨。無子，除。

translations.literal: Gaoping: Prince Huai Jian Ji Ye, the second son by a secondary consort of Prince Gong, was enfeoffed at the beginning of Yongle. He died in the fifth year. He had no sons; [the line was] abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoping: Prince Huai Jian Ji Ye, Prince Gong's second son by a secondary consort, was enfeoffed early in Yongle. He died in Yongle 5 without issue; the line was abolished.

cells.content: 平陽 濟熿，恭庶三子，永樂初封。十二年，晉王濟熺廢，遂襲晉封。宣德二年通高煦事發，革爵，發高牆，除。

translations.literal: Pingyang: Ji Huang, the third son by a secondary consort of Prince Gong, was enfeoffed at the beginning of Yongle. In the twelfth year, after Prince of Jin Ji Xi was deposed, he succeeded to the Jin fief. In the second year of Xuande his collusion with Gao Xu was exposed; his rank was stripped, he was sent to the high walls, and [the line was] abolished.

translations.literal: Qingcheng: Prince Zhuang Hui Ji Xuan, the fourth son by a secondary consort of Prince Gong, was enfeoffed in the first year of Yongle with a separate seat at Fenzhou. He died in the fourth year of Xuande.

translations.literal: Prince Rong Duan Biao ?, the lone son by the principal consort of Prince Rong Xi, succeeded to the fief as Defender-of-the-State General in the fifth year of Zhengde. He died in the sixth year. He had no sons. Prince Duan He Biao ?, the lone son by a secondary consort of Prince Gong Jian, advanced from Defender-of-the-State General in the twenty-sixth year of Jiajing. As a younger cousin inheriting his elder brother's title, he confessed to usurped enfeoffment; [the line] was not to inherit again. He died in the fourth year of Longqing; [the line was] abolished.
